chunks: From him, from al-Qasim, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about selling gold for dirhams, and he said: 'Send a messenger so that he may take full payment for you.' He said: 'He says: Give and come, and your messenger will be with him.'

key_terms.هَاتِ وَهَلُمَّ: Give and come (imperatives indicating immediate exchange)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for selling gold for silver according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of *qabd* (possession) in gold-for-silver exchanges by specifying that a messenger must physically take possession of the full amount, thereby ensuring the transaction is not merely a debt offset but a completed sale. This detail addresses the scholarly debate on whether *qabd* requires actual physical transfer or if constructive possession suffices, emphasizing the necessity of removing *gharar* (uncertainty) through immediate control. The ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on practical execution of contractual conditions to prevent the subtle forms of *riba* prohibited in Islamic jurisprudence.
